newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips jump to fifth straight record. [CORRECTED 22:21 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Blue chips jump to fifth straight record. [CORRECTED 22:21 GMT]

text.p: Stocks set records for the fifth straight session Thursday as a report of weak retail sales last month convinced investors the Federal Reserve was unlikely to raise interest rates next month.

According to early, unofficial results, the Dow Jones industrial average jumped 135.20 points, or 1.78 percent, to close at 7,711.03, two days after closing above 7,500 for the first time. Other market averages also rose, though the gains were generally smaller, with the Nasdaq index up 3.48 points, or 0.25 percent, at 1,411.33.
(Corrects from "four days" in headline; from "a day after closing above 7,500...")
